In all of our lives there is that one person that is so special you would never do anything to hurt them. Whether that person be a close friend, a significant other, or a family member. The people that are involved in our lives significantly are there to help us through the rough patches, bring us up when we are down, and be there for us. Friends are one of the most important people we have in life. Friends are someone we can talk to and they understand, someone we share everything with including clothes, food, etc. They are the ones that get us through each day with a smile. High school is filled with drama, it's the same old story just, a different day. I have the best group of friends, we are very close and spend a lot of time with each other at school and outside of school. They are there for me when I need them the most. Recently this guy, and I have been trying to work on our relationship but he had been lying to me and cheating on me but everyone of my friends that I talk to abut the situation say the same thing, "he is going to hurt you" and "he's not worth your tears." I have class with him every other day. It's not like I get to choose when I want and don't want to see him, some days are just better than others. The bell rang, right after lunch, and I wasn't in any hurry to get to the band room. The band room is very big, smells like old cheese and is like a trampoline for sound to bounce off of and explode in your face. I don't enjoy that class at all. I walked in the room nonchalantly and set all my books on my chair and began walking to my cubby. I grabbed my instrument walked back to set it on my chair and went to talk with some of my friends. It hadn't been a bad day so far, it was just a regular day at school. Entering the band room I had a feeling that was different. He walked through the band door with a huge smile on his face but I couldn't help but look away and frown. Mixed emotions are the worst, he does one thing and you love him and he does another thing that drives you insane and makes you want to hurt him. He sits right behind me in band and I am constantly turning around to talk to him but we never seem to get in trouble except for , we were supposedly talking to much. I don't believe we were talking to much, because was where I wanted nothing to do with him. He was upset with me and I was upset with him, so we were even. Twenty-five minutes passed by, each minute dragging on longer and all I was thinking about was him and what I had heard he was doing. It's never a good feeling when you know something is wrong. I confronted him about what people were telling me. His response was "don't believe what you hear, believe what you see." I didn't know what was going on, but tears started pouring out of my eyes, running down my face like a crystal clear waterfall. I asked my teacher if i could take a minute out in the hall, and she agreed, so I sat in the hall, with tears running down my face. One of my friends walked out the door and sat with me to comfort me. We started talking and I told her everything that was going on. She gave me a hug, and start making jokes about him. I couldn't help but laugh. I even smiled and made my own remarks that got her to laugh as well. After a few jokes, and a bunch of hugs, the tears went away and I was smiling. Neither of us wanted to go back in class but we didn't really have any other options. We weren't very close friends, but our talk during class, made us grow stronger. Even when everything is going wrong, you should count on your friends to tell you the truth, and give their advice, because they are always right so don't second guess them. They know how to make you feel better and it always seems to work. Laughter is much more than an emotion. It gives you strength when you are weak. It builds you up when you are down. Laughter brings relationships closer, and sometimes all we need is to smile. Laughter also helps create memories, the nights you stay up talking and laughing until two in the morning are the ones you will remember forever. Laughter is an important aspect to everyone, we all need a day to just relax and take a step back to laugh.

Just before break, in the fourth grade, there was a party at my neighbors house. My parents and I were invited, and since we didnt have plans, we decided to go to the party. The party was spectacular! There were stockings hung over the fireplace, green and red streamers everywhere, and huge tree in the living room. Under the tree, there was a large pile of presents-each one for the children. My neighbor saw me staring at the presents, so he walked over, picked up a present, and handed it to me. The present was a rectangular shape wrapped in blue gift wrap decorated with snowflakes. On the front was my name in marker. I was about to open my present when my neighbor told me to wait. He said that if I opened it now, I would only get one gift. If I waited until morning to open it, I would get two gifts. I didnt understand it at first, but he said I soon would. was a week away! How in the world was I suppose to wait until then? Of course I wanted two gifts, so I told my neighbor I would wait. Deep down inside though, I wanted to tear the present right open. The days dragged on. Why was the week going by so slowly? As drew near, I grew impatient. I almost opened my present three days before . Inside was a note: only have you earned yourself a new diary, you now have the gift of patience. Now I understood.

Learning to laugh as we were vacationing in , I realized that laughter is a big part of our lives, and an important factor that can keep friends and families together. Not too long ago I also discovered that laughter can relieve you from stress, and it even helps you lose weight, which, I thought was pretty interesting. My sister on the other hand still did not quite believe that laughter could do all of that. She thought it was just being blown out of proportion. She believed that if her friends didn't want to hang around with her, then there was something wrong with them, that if we didn't have enough food in the house, it was probably my parents fault. There was always some one to blame for whatever happened to her, there was always a bad side to everything. But that it was going to be different she was about to find out that she didn't have to live her live that way, because there is always an alternative. The trip to was something everyone was expecting, even me. I was actually really excited to see my cousins and the rest of the family. Everybody packed their things, we got ready to leave, got on the car and left to the air port. My aunt was already waiting for us at the city airport. Everything was going great. So far... When we got there, my aunt drove all of us to our little town in the state of , just about an hour and a half away from the airport. As we were getting there I noticed my sister had a strange look on her face, she seemed somehow confused, lost in her own thoughts as if she was worried about something."'s wrong with you, are you okay? you look all weird..." I said sounding a little sarcastic and hoping to start a conversation." face is all weird!"she said and that was the thing she said to me until we reached our destination. As we got to our grandparents house we begun to see all our family members already waiting for us outside. The joy of seeing them there was incredible. I looked around around and i saw my sister, I was glad that she looked happy, i thought she was actually enjoying the moment. I did not know was wrong with her and her sudden attitude changes until we got to the little playground my grandma has in the backyard. During my time there I met new family members, saw some old familiar faces and remembered some good and also bad memories, memories which I thought had vanished from my mind already. Turns out they were still there, all the way at the back of my head were I had tried to hide them so that they would never come up again, but somehow they managed to get out and make their way into my thoughts again, and that is when I started to feel like a monster once again. Suddenly I had a flash back to the time when we came to visit, a couple of years ago. That's when it all came to me i saw the whole scene once again I felt horrible. There she was, my little sister playing in the swings, suddenly she let go of the swing and she felt right into a mud puddle that was there. Every body laughed, I laughed. I thought it was funny, but she didn't laugh, she didn't cry either, she just got up and ran inside. I never stopped to ask her if she was okay, I didn't realize how my actions had affected her. It was all my fault, I knew she was really sensitive when it came down to some specific situations, but I did not help her, I didn't give her the comfort and support she needed from her big sister, so she never learned to laugh at herself and keep going. That would have been a nice advice to give her instead of laughing at her. Then, after a couple of minutes of reflection about it, I went up to her and apologized, she looked a little confused at first, but then she realized where i was going. This made the rest of the trip a lot more easier, now that I knew was wrong, we both tried our best to fix the problem and work on her self esteem. Laughter was the perfect therapy for her. All she needed to do was to learn how to laugh about her self when things did not go the way she wanted them. It was hard but we accomplished our goal. My sister discovered the power of laughter, and she learned to get back up from her mistakes. Life taught both of us an important lesson that . I'm sure that was one of the most exciting trips we've ever taken and the memories from that trip will stay with us forever.

Честно говоря, самая острая проблема в нашем ауле — это качество воды в скважинах. Живу я в Шиели уже 19 лет, и вижу, как это влияет на здоровье людей. Вода из большинства скважин содержит слишком много солей и минералов, особенно летом. Моя бабушка Гульнара постоянно жалуется на проблемы с почками, соседи болеют чаще обычного.

Проблема системная. Во-первых, скважины старые, некоторым больше 30 лет. Во-вторых, нет современной системы очистки. В-третьих, местное население просто не знает о вреде, люди пьют эту воду и думают, что это нормально.

Я хочу это решить, потому что изучаю Public Policy and Development и понимаю, что здоровье — основа развития. Когда люди болеют, они не могут работать, учиться, развивать бизнес. Мой план включает три шага: первый — провести анализ воды во всех скважинах ауле вместе с лабораторией из Кызылорды, второй — написать грант в акимат, третий — установить фильтры в общественных местах и провести образовательную кампанию.

Мне кажется, если решить проблему воды, весь аул поднимется на новый уровень развития. Это не просто мои интересы — это благо для всех.

Middle school was a challenging environment. Not only are kids subjected to a rapid advancement in the academic environment, but a maturing social environment as well. The rapidly growing need for social dominance and in turn inflating egos makes for a bully breeding ground. Without the skill to be able to laugh it off, I would fear for anyone's mental well being in that environment. Throughout my first years in middle school, I struggled with the building social discomfort of classmates higher in the social chain, making for a severe toll not only my self-esteem, but my academics as well. The stress of my own social stature plummeted my grades continuing a cycle resulting in even more stress. The whole situation seemed hopeless and depressing. I could not believe that in only a little over a decade of life, my outlook had become so grim. I wondered how I would make it through the rest my school years. Everyday I had the pleasure of hearing any number of new insults made up by those higher in the social ladder, attempting to supplement their growing self-esteem and inflating egos; some days even those who I previously believed to be my friends joined in with them. Except for a few trusted companions, it seemed the whole world was out to further themselves by bashing me with any number of new insults. Being made fun of daily had continued until I realized something; That laughter is key in social survival. Without laughter there was no way I could have survived those school years. After this revelation I was able to laugh at things said to me and laugh at myself as well. I was able to take the the cacophony and learn with it, taking it as critique to better myself. Through laughter and their jarring remarks I was able to secure my position in the social scheme as well as improve my intelligence, as well as make new, better friends and come to peace with others, while maintaining the the hurt I experienced earlier to be "popular" without having to make fun out of those who were like who I used to be; a win-win scenario. Laughter is key in any situation, whether it be a conversation with a friend, or experiencing the penned up frustrations of immature adolescents. From laughter I learned a great lesson, one that I hope everyone has not learned should. Without the lesson of laughter, I don't know how anyone could lead a successful and pleasurable life.

Честно говоря, самый большой вызов для меня был переход с казахского языка на английский когда я поступил в университет. В школе номер 15 в Кызылорде мы учили английский, но не на таком уровне. Когда начались лекции в программе Leadership and Innovation, я просто терялся на занятиях. Первые два месяца было реально тяжело. Я сидел в библиотеке после занятий, смотрел видео на YouTube, учил слова по три часа в день. Мой сосед по общежитию Айтжан посоветовал присоединиться к языковому клубу при университете, где встречаются студенты и практикуют разговорный английский. Моя большая цель – запустить собственное приложение для управления логистикой в нефтегазовой отрасли к концу 2025 года. Это актуально для Атырау, потому что здесь куча компаний в нефтяной сфере, а толковых решений не хватает.

Я разбил это на конкретные этапы. Сейчас учусь на программе IT Product Design в колледже, параллельно прохожу курсы по UI/UX дизайну на Coursera. К апрелю 2024 года хочу закончить прототип приложения. К августу – собрать команду из двух разработчиков и одного маркетолога. К декабрю – провести тестирование с реальными клиентами.

Столкнулся с проблемой – мой русский язык для общения с иностранными партнёрами был слаб. Решил это просто: три месяца занимался с репетитором Светланой Викторовной онлайн. Теперь свободно общаюсь на English.

Второе препятствие – финансирование. Я начал фриланс на Fiverr, делаю дизайны для малых компаний. За полгода заработал 150 тысяч тенге на разработку MVP. Это реальная помощь для моего проекта.

Сейчас у меня готов дизайн первой версии, два потенциальных инвестора уже смотрели презентацию. Это мотивирует идти дальше.

У нас в Creative Engineering была крутая задача на втором семестре – разработать мобильное приложение для туристов, которые приезжают в Тараз. Я была в команде с Мадияром, он отвечал за программирование, и Аней, которая делала дизайн. Четвёртым был Батыр из группы – он занимался маркетингом и исследованием рынка.

На начальном этапе произошёл конфликт. Аня хотела сделать интерфейс максимально красивым с анимациями, а Мадияр говорил, что это замедлит приложение и будет тяжело на старых телефонах. Я предложила провести встречу в кафе "Нур" возле университета и вместе обсудить приоритеты. Батыр показал данные – большинство пользователей в Казахстане используют бюджетные смартфоны, поэтому оптимизация критична.

Моя роль была как раз в этом – быть связующим звеном между визионом и реальностью. Я помогала переводить технические ограничения в дизайнерские решения. Мы нашли компромисс: красивый, но оптимизированный дизайн.

В итоге приложение получилось намного лучше, чем если бы каждый работал отдельно. Оно действительно используется туристами в Таразе, и это было невозможно без того, чтобы мы слушали друг друга и вместе решали проблемы.

When I was a young boy I used to laugh at anything I could, but as a kid who didn't? As I got older and grew more, I developed a great sense of humor that to my advantage made me a young people pleas-er. I grew more and more developing a stronger, more confident sense of humor. I could always remember making people laugh and loving the attention I received from humor. As my body grew older and my humor grew more funny I had made myself more dependent on my people pleasing personality. In addition, I then taught myself how to alter my voice and change my tone for a more humorous effect. It was a step I knew was appropriate to advance my humorous personality. I had no intention of loosing my humor, so I used it to my advantage. I used my humor to boost my count, to get attention from non-accepting peers, and to get the attention that I thrived on. I had began to be accepted by higher peer groups that used to look down on me and it seemed as if I had a lot of the attention. Anything I could do to make my fellow peers laugh was a goal for me. Anything from rolling down stairs, telling jokes, making teachers angry which students thought was funny, and occasionally destroying things. All this just so I could fit into the crowd that used to reject me. As I advanced into high school I knew my humor needed work to keep my peers still laughing, I just didn't know what kind of work I needed. That was when I started to ultimately loose my funny, humorous personality. I had then dropped in the peer ranks, down to the kids I thought were once called strange. I was friends with people who didn't always keep their heads up and were constantly down and seemed never positive. I was letting people that I called friends drag me to the bottom when I knew I should be more at the top. This was my first major downfall in which I had successfully lost my humorous personality. One of my friends especially brought me down more than anyone else, down to a father level of being unhappy. That so called "" took me down so far that I needed therapy to help me get back up to a normal level of happiness. I finally realized that it wasn't fun to be someones who only drags you down. I finally broke free of that clutch when she moved, I wasn't mean enough to say I didn't wanna be friends with her, it was just to hard for me. When she moved it allowed me to heal myself and pay more attention to my humor. I had broke my dark days away and started back on my endless trail of humor. It was hard to accept the fact that I had lost my humor for what seemed to be forever, and lost my spot in the social bracket which would be hard to regain. But after a month of hard work and focus on both school and humor I had got my personality back to normal! Instantly after I regained my humor I began to feel more happy. I received more attention and felt like I was back to were I should be, although I was just a little lower. Back in the saddle of humor, back the laughs of my peers, back to the smiles, and most importantly back to the way I used to be. I had to regain all of my humor and personality, my tones, voices, and jokes but it was worth it, in a strange way. As I now continue my humor as a junior and I have not successfully lost it yet, but there is always a future. I managed to turn the best thing I had to the worst I have felt in a matter of weeks, then right back up again. In the end its not what you have that matters it is what you can do to please yourself and in the end I would not change a thing!

There is simply some material that is not appropriate for children, and it should not be put in our public libraries. Not censoring what is put on the shelves seems obsurd considering my experience. If I have a son someday, I want to be the one telling him about the touchy subjects of women and swearing; it should not be from some fiction book. I also do not appreciate the other material found in our libraries. The music that I see has artists that write their songs without children in mind, movies have up to ratings, and magazines promote gossip and have sexual references. Overall, it is disappointing to me that our libraries have allowed some of these things onto their shelves. As I think about my experience in third grade, I wish I had never seen that book. Maybe it would have allowed me to keep a little more innocense for a little bit longer, and maybe I would have respected women more through my youth. I would love to see more censorship in libraries so that we can protect today's children until the parents choose to open their eyes to the world.

Моя главная цель – запустить собственное digital-агентство к концу 2025 года. Это не просто мечта, а реальный план, над которым я активно работаю прямо сейчас.

В начале года я поставил себе задачу: к сентябрю получить первых трёх клиентов и заработать минимум 500 тысяч тенге. Сейчас уже август, и я на пути к этому. Моя стратегия простая – начал с фриланса на платформах, потом перешёл на прямые контракты с местными бизнесами в Уральске.

Первый клиент – это кафе «Мастер» на улице Достоевского. Я делал им SMM-стратегию и увеличил их инстаграм с 800 до 4500 подписчиков за три месяца. Второй клиент – салон красоты «Королева» на проспекте Абулхаир-хана. Сейчас работаю с ними над контент-планом.

Главное препятствие было в недостатке опыта. Я решил это, пройдя курсы у Марата Кужахметова, известного казахстанского маркетолога. Потратил 150 тысяч, но это окупилось уже на первом проекте.

На учёбе в ВУЗе совмещаю всё это с расписанием, иногда сложно, но мотивирует то, что вижу реальные результаты. К 2026 году планирую иметь команду из 3-4 человек и месячный доход 2 миллиона тенге.

Лидерство для меня – это не просто командовать людьми, а вдохновлять их и двигаться вместе к цели. Я понимаю это через свой опыт в Creative Engineering на втором курсе.

В прошлом году мы работали над проектом робота-манипулятора для школьной выставки. Наша группа состояла из шести человек, и честно говоря, в начале было сложно. Ребята были разбросаны – кто-то занимался только программированием, кто-то только механикой, никто не знал, как всё это соединить.

Я предложила еженедельные встречи в кафе "Астана" возле колледжа, где мы вместе обсуждали прогресс каждого. Не приказывала, а слушала, что думает каждый. Например, Ерлан предложил использовать Arduino вместо более сложной платы – это сэкономило бюджет. Я поддержала эту идею и помогла ему объяснить остальным, почему это хорошее решение.

Наш робот в итоге занял второе место на областной выставке в Павлодаре. Это был не огромный успех, но команда почувствовала себя единым целым. Каждый понял, что его голос важен.

Вот это для меня лидерство – не звёзды на погонах, а способность объединить людей и помочь им поверить в себя.

Честно говоря, меня очень беспокоит проблема с туризмом и культурным наследием в нашем городе. Туркестан – это такое важное место для всего Казахстана, но туристы часто не знают, куда идти, что смотреть. Информация разбросана по разным сайтам, половина на казахском, половина на английском, и всё запутанно.

Я вижу это постоянно. Приезжают люди в Туркестан, ходят только к мавзолею Ходжа Ахмета Йассауи, потом уезжают. А ведь у нас есть музей истории, крепость, медресе – столько всего интересного! Местные гиды теряют заработки, бизнесмены не получают прибыль, а туристы не видят настоящий Туркестан.

Я бы создал интерактивное приложение на казахском, русском и английском языках с картой всех достопримечательностей, рейтингами, отзывами местных. Туда же добавить маршруты разной сложности – на день, на выходные. Партнёрство с отелями и кафе типа «Керуен» или «Samal Sanatoria».

На своей программе Digital Media я как раз учусь такому. Мой друг Арман уже помогает в туристическом агентстве его отца – вижу, как много времени уходит на координацию. Это реально нужно нашему городу. Туризм развивает экономику, создаёт рабочие места, и люди узнают нашу историю лучше.

Честно говоря, самый большой вызов для меня был переход на английский язык во время учёбы в университете. Когда я поступил на Public Policy and Development три года назад, все лекции были на английском, а мой уровень был максимум intermediate. Первый семестр был сложным – я не понимал половину того, что говорил профессор Дмитрий на семинарах по политологии.

Помогло мне несколько вещей. Во-первых, я начал смотреть фильмы и подкасты на английском каждый день, сидя в кафе «Арай» рядом с университетом. Во-вторых, мой одногруппник Нурлан, который хорошо говорит по-английски, согласился заниматься со мной два раза в неделю. Мы разбирали конспекты и обсуждали лекции на английском, что было очень эффективно.

Также помогла дополнительная онлайн-программа на Coursera, которую я проходил летом 2022 года. Преподаватели в университете заметили мой прогресс и стали более терпеливы на занятиях. К концу второго года я уже без проблем писал эссе и участвовал в дискуссиях.

Сейчас я понимаю, что главное – это не сдаваться и искать помощь у людей. Это простой урок, но очень важный для моего развития.

Моя главная цель — к концу этого года получить сертификат по проектному менеджменту и запустить свой стартап в сфере водных ресурсов. Это очень актуально для Балхаша, где озеро постоянно мелеет, а экологические проблемы становятся острее.

Я разбил это на этапы. Во-первых, до сентября нужно закончить онлайн-курс на Coursera — уже прошёл половину модулей. Во-вторых, к октябрю собрать команду из трёх человек. Ещё была проблема с финансированием идеи, но наш куратор Алексей Викторович помог мне подать заявку на грант от местного акимата. Ждём результата в августе.

Libraries have a variety of material from books to movies. Most of this is intended for a general audience and many people can read or watch whatever they want. Some of the literature and other material you find in libraries however, are not intended for certain people, such as young children. Censorship takes material that these certian people should not read away from everyone. Many people want censorship not just in libraries but in many aspects of life. Censorship is not bad per say but it does restrict people, who would normally have access to a certain topic, to a general catigory. Not everyone likes to read the same thing as someone else. Other then likes and dislikes is the problem of offensiveness. Everyone finds something offensive. The idea of the removal of 'offensive' material from libraries is understandable. Some believe that this material is not appropriate for anyone to view. However, because we all have different opinions on what is offensive, I believe that books found to be offensive should not be removed from the shelves of the library. First, I believe that if this policy were to be in effect in libraries, there would not be many books left on the shelf. Offensive is a relative word. What be offensive to one person not be to another. Every has a different opinion on different matters based on their beliefs and life experiences. Many books have things people disagree with, but expressing this is a part of freedom of speech. Therefore, if everyone complained that they found a certain book or movie to be offensive, there would hardly be anything left, as Katherine Paterson said. The purpose of a library is to provide the people who go to the library a resource. If the sources were censored in such a way, it would be hard to get information. Sometimes, it is beneficial, even, to read an opposing view or side to have more knowledge on a certain topic and see things from a different perspective. However, some books not be entirely appropriate to certain people. For example, some material in the library not be best for small children to read or view. In this case, I do not necessarily feel that they should be removed from the shelves rather than placed in an area these children do not have access to. Having books, music, movies, or magazines removed from the shelves if they are found to be offensive is in my opinion, a ridiculous notion. It hinders expression. People have different opinions about what is offensive to them and it would be very boring if everyone thought the same. If someone finds something particularly offensive, I believe they just should not view it

Честно говоря, самый большой вызов для меня был переход в десятый класс. Я учился в школе номер 7 в Семее, и когда надо было выбирать направление, я запаниковал. Все мои друзья знали, куда они хотят идти, а я был в полной растерянности. Родители давили, говорили, что надо выбирать что-то серьезное, перспективное.

Я помню, как сидел в библиотеке нашей школы и просто не знал, что делать. Потом наша классный руководитель Айгуль Кабдулловна предложила мне посетить информационный день в Торайгыров университета. Там я встретил студента Дениса, который учился на программе Public Policy and Development. Он рассказал мне про направление, про то, как можно помогать людям через политику и развитие общества. Это как-то щелкнуло во мне.

После этого я стал более уверенно готовиться к поступлению. Помогли мне также мой брат Ерлан, который поступил в медицинский, и репетитор по истории Марина Ивановна. Они верили, что я справлюсь. Честно, это был не очень сложный вызов, но он научил меня не бояться просить помощи и слушать людей, которые знают больше.

Ну, у нас в университете был проект по социологии в прошлом семестре. Мы делали исследование о влиянии соцсетей на молодёжь Шымкента. В нашей группе было четыре человека: я, Айдар, Жанара и Ерлан.

Честно говоря, в начале было сложновато. Каждый предлагал свой подход, и мы не сразу нашли общий язык. Я больше занимался организацией опроса среди студентов КазНУ и ТарГУ. Ездил в кампусы, раздавал анкеты, потом вводил данные в Excel. Айдар с Ераланом делали анализ, а Жанара писала теоретическую часть.

На середине проекта выяснилось, что у нас много пропусков в данных. Пришлось пересчитывать выборку. Я вместе с Айдаром переделали половину опросов в районе парка Абая и возле ТРЦ «Shymkent Plaza». Было утомительно, но нужно было.

В итоге мы сдали проект вовремя, получили оценку хорошую. Преподаватель Баян Анаровна отметила качество сбора данных. Я понял, что в командной работе важно не просто делать свою часть, но и помогать другим, когда что-то идёт не так. Это был полезный опыт для нас всех.

Have you ever been laughing at something that someone said, and then began laughing harder at, not the joke, but at a person whose laugh was almost more humorous than the joke itself? Then were you put into a good mood after the funny laughing occurred, when just before that you could have been in the world's worst mood? Laughter is the cure for almost anything from being in a bad mood to crying because you're sad. It can also help make the mood in the room brighter or simply it makes any awkward moment disappear. One bright day, called me and asked if I wanted to long board down to 's and get some lunch with her. Of course I wanted to because I'm always up for my typical 's order of a chocolate malt milkshake and some croutons and ranch. I jogged to her house down the block and we long boarded down to 's in downtown . On the way to 's I shared with how I had not had a good day so far and how I needed to be cheered up. She was feeling the same way. When we arrived at 's we were both excited to get seated so we could catch up with each others lives and eat. When we walked inside we noticed how crowded it seemed to be that day as we waited for a table. After getting seated we noticed an older couple sitting in the booth behind us, some kids from our school in the booth front of us, and a man and women across the aisle. ordered a strawberry milkshake and a burger with fries, and I ordered my usual. After the lady took our order and left, and I started telling each other the reasons for our bad moods. She was in a bad mood because her friend was not treating her right. I was in a bad mood because my friend was mad at me for something that never happened. We were both quite upset and frankly we were in no laughing mood. When all of a sudden we heard what sounded like a mixture of a goose's honking and a donkey's braying. We turned around to find it was a lady's laughter. I looked at and she looked at me and we started busting up laughing. This went on for about minutes straight. We both could not believe a sound like that could come out of any human being's mouth and it was probably the loudest laugh I've ever heard. We also loved the fact that all of this is happening at a public place with all these people around, and the lady was just setting herself up for being made fun of. and I continued to laugh at the lady for how she was laughing and it somehow started to relieve our bad moods. started smiling a little more and as for me, I couldn't stop smiling and laughing. Laughter has an unusual way of putting people in a good mood or relieving them of their bad moods. Regardless if the laugh is a normal little chuckle or an unnatural sound coming out of someone's mouth, laughter brings people together and it's great way to turn a awkward moment into a memorable moment. Someone once said, "laughter is the shortest distance between two people," and that person knew what they were talking about.

It seems as if inappropriate materials are found everywhere in today's world. In magazines, in books, in the lyrics of music, the possibilities of where to sneak in offensive references are endless, and they certainly pop up everywhere these days. But should your resources of where you find these materials be limited due to other people's morals or values? I disagree with this act, and I would like to tell you why I do. All of us have different morals, values, and sences of what is right and what is wrong; everyone's are different. Maybe it's your religion or culture that keep you from these materials. But why should your values and beliefs dictate what another person can or cannot get from their library? I know I don't just speak for myself when I say I would be very annoyed if I couldn't get the books or materials I wanted or needed just because the person next to me doesn't agree with what is being found through researching it. I do believe certain things should be seperated from other parts of the libraries. For example, books that would be found offensive to children should be kept away from where children can pick out things in a library. That is completely understandable. But when things are being removed because certain peolpe don't agree with them or find them offensive, that is when things are going too far. This nation was built on the grounds of freedom for what you believe in. So why should we force others to believe something we think? Just because I find something offensive, doesn't mean the person next to me does, which is completely fine with me. That is his or her own personal opinion, and what I believe should not keep him or her from learning about the things they would like to. One way to fix this problem would be to seperate things that could possibly be found offensive into another section of the library and to put out a sign or paper saying what exactly can be found in that section. In conclusion, no, I do not think libraries should be censored. I know I could walk into my local library and find things I found offensive right now, but I would not want my own opinion to effect someone else's viewing of that material. People should think about one another once in a while and not be so stuck on what they personally believe. The world is an opinionated place, if it were not we would have nothing. A library can be filled with usful materials, so the focus should be on what you can find in a library to help you, not on what is in the library that you do not want to see. If you find something offensive, simply stay away from it, but don't try to take it away from the rest of the world.

Have you ever got a detention from laughing an inordinate amount in class? If you haven't, you're very lucky. I know that teachers absolutely hate students that don't pay attention in class, or students that will randomly start laughing when they're giving a lecture. I'm that student that will randomly bust up laughing (preferably at my own jokes) in class. In other words, I'm a teachers worst nightmare. Ring....ring....ring, time for . It was a beautiful afternoon and I was feeling great! When I walked into the class, I automatically noticed that our teacher wasn't his blessedly self. But I ignored it and went on with what I normally do, which is get out my and crank up the tunes. I like to listen to music because it relaxes me and helps me focus more. The downside to listening to music is that you can't exactly hear everything that great. When I listen to music I have those moments when I feel like I'm in a movie that everything seems like it's in slow motion but you can't hear anything. It's almost like I'm secluded in my own little world and no one can see me or hear me, until I start laughing that is. Finally class started and everyone was being abnormally loud, at this point I was starting to see the steam come out of our teachers ears. He looked like a cartoon character off of bugs bunny. The teacher was getting very indignant and impatient with the class. I didn't exactly pay much attention to him so I went back to listening to my music. After a while, our teacher was now starting to get frenzied with the class even more so he told everyone whoever talks again will get their name written up on the board and you will receive detention. About five minutes later my friend comes and walks by me and starts talking to me. When I listen to music, I have a tendency to talk loud because I feel like they can't even hear me. So I start yelling, and she starts to giggle because when I wasn't looking my teacher was just staring at me wondering why I was talking so loud. He turns around and writes my name on the board (that meant I was given a warning). I turn to look at the teacher, oh no here it comes, my laughter is out, I couldn't control myself. When I laugh uncontrollably, I laugh like there's no tomorrow. "! You owe me thirty minutes of detention!" said my teacher. One of the biggest problems that I have is I'm very easily amused, I laugh at mainly everything and anything. When my teacher yelled at me, his facial expression was just way too funny, so I began to laugh even harder. When I start laughing, my friend usually can't help herself but start laughing with me. She tells the teacher that she was the one that made me laugh so she thought she deserved detention too. So she got what she wanted, detention! One week later, and I arrived in good old detention with all the other "rebels" (that's what I call myself now) it makes me feel tough. The thing that we have learned is that we should never be sitting next to each other. When we sit by each other, we can't stop laughing, but we decided to sit by each other anyways. What do you know, we almost got more detention while in detention, imagine that. "'s to short to live with tension and regrets, so just laugh it off!" That motto is what I try to live by everyday. I feel like laughing is a very important part in my , it really helps me forget what is bothering me. Even though I get in trouble from laughing, I don't regret it one bit. Some people are very serious and they don't know how to let things go so they're always tense. Laughing releases tension and for me I feel like it brings me closer to my friends. I love laughing with my friends and the feeling of your abs hurting from laughing is awesome!Live your live, laugh as much as you can, and love those that mean the most to you.

A is a wondrous gift. It allows your mind and your body to conjoin with others. It is the root of happiness, and brings a sense of sanity to those who have lost hope. When you feel alone in the world with no one at your side, laughter will be there to accompany you. At one point in my life I felt confused and by myself. I was empty. Solitude was the only thing I could have, and the only feeling my mind would register. Just when I had thought that I be the only person in the whole world, something had come to save me. I was six years old when they got divorced. I couldn't stand to hear my parents fight. One day we were the perfect family. We would play board games and go to the movies together. Something had changed very quickly. My grabbed his jacket, told me he loved me and then he was gone. Was I ever going to see him again? Why isn't living with us? These are questions I kept asking myself. I think i was too young to truly know what was going on. The days were long and I found myself becoming sluggish and glum. About two weeks after my had left, some neighbors moved into the house adjacent to me and my mom. One of the neighbors looked young, about my age. I didn't think much of the new people in town. I told myself that people come and go. Nothing lasts forever, and I should expect the worst. One day I was riding my bike and thought that I should stop pedaling and crash into my fence. I asked the boy his name and he didn't respond; though he did start to laugh again. It was my voice that he was laughing at. Everything I did caused him to become hysterical. I found out later that he was from and didn't speak a word of . Over the course of a month or so, I felt the hole in my heart begin to fill. My new companion and his laugh was the start to my new beginning. My mom and I eventually moved out of our house and lost contact with the neighbors. I am always reminded of him when I hear a laugh. Though he's not near me in a physical sense, I am guided by his laughter every day.

Although I would have found it slighly rude, another person have found it to be a nice compliment. With this logic, can one really conclude that anything is truely offensive? By saying something is offensive, you're stating your own opinion. Even if they aren't the same as everyone else's, everyone is intitled to their own opinions; equality is something most people find very important. Because of this, one person's definiton of offensive shouldn't be held higher than another's. If we rid libraries of 'offensive' material, that is exactly what you would be doing; you'd be making one person's definition of offensive superior to another person's. I also believe libraries should not get rid of 'offensive' material because by doing so, they would probably be getting rid of a lot of interesting material. Let's use my religious beliefs for an example. I am . Basically, I do not believe in ''. If someone were to write a book about my religion, I would find it interesting. Some find it to be offensive, though. So if a library got rid of that book because someone found it offensive, I wouldn't want to go there as often. When I go to a library, I want to find a book that I'd enjoy reading. If all the material that is found offensive was taken out of the library, would there really be anything left? If so, I doubt many people would find it interesting. I also believe this because by taking a book off the shelf because you find it offensive, wouldn't you be offending the author? As I said before, everyone is intitled to their own opinions. Because of this, libraries should allow authors to speak their minds. By taking their books off the shelves, you'd be offending them. They took their time and effort to think about and write that book, and for you to offend them by taking it off the shelf, you'd be controdicting the entire purpose of removing it from the shelf. In conclusion, I believe that nothing can truely be defined as offensive. Also, people should be able to speak their minds. Therefore, libraries should not attempt to rid there shelves of 'offensive' material

In todays world, children are exposed to a lot of inappropriate things than in recent times. They hear things from older siblings, see uncensored programs on television, hear words in music, and even learn things from books. An issue at hand is whether or not libraries should or should not dispose of inappropriate books, movies, music, and magazines. Children can read whatever they like if their parents give permission, but in today's society some parents do not take the time to care, consumed in their work. One way society can take care of this problem is setting age limits on books. There have been times when my mother will not allow me to read a book because it dealt with issues that I was not ready to learn about. Although I am lucky that my mother cares about what I read, some parents are not. This is why an age limit would be helpful in keeping our youth modest. The librarians, or a national book association, could decide if the content of a book is appropriate for a certain age. This would take care of children reading about bawdy issues that they should not know about. Also, books should be more readily available. These types of books teach good morals and how to live a good and full life. In schools across the country, many authors are not in the public school libraries. By putting these types of books into the libraries, students would be more aware of them and would most likely have an interest in them, learning from them. Another issue libraries have is music and movies. It is nice to be able to go to the library and check out a cd or even a movie. But, some of these have terrible language and scenes not appropriate for children. What can the general public do about this? Well, demand that all music and videos with content not generalized for children be removed from the libraries. This would keep children from seeing and hearing actions they should not copy. There are ratings on movies for a reason, so why not use them. Anything above should be a definent no in libraries. If the movie has content that any child under thirteen should not see, then the movie should be out. Magazines also offer a source of learning. Some are very educational, and give the students ideas to go and come up with a new invention or a way to help others. But, some have content that are not suited for children. Thus, like the books, the magazines should also have ratings. The magazine , for example, has articles that are to bawdy for students to read. Magazines like this should be put in an adult section where students cannot look at them. Magazines also offer pictures that, in recent times, would have been illegal to put out. But, in today's standards, they are fine to put in magazines. These magazines should not even be allowed in the libraries across our nation. America's standards on what is okay to read, look at, watch, and listen to have changed drastically. Children are learning things they should not know about, until an older age, at a very young age. Society need to put strict restrictions on what is right and what is not for children. I personally believe that there should be very strict restrictions on what children are allowed to watch, read, and listen to. My parents were very strict about this and, in the end, I feel this has benefitted my learning process. Also, I feel the libraries should rid of books that, in olden times, would have been a shame to read. Parents today are not as in sync with what their children do as they were in recent years. So, society needs to put a strict rule on what libraries carry and what they do not.

Честно говоря, самый сложный период был в десятом классе, когда я почти не поступил в Creative Engineering. Я готовился к экзамену по математике целый год, занимался с репетитором Асланом три раза в неделю. Но на первой попытке получил 68 баллов — это было ниже проходного порога на 12 пунктов.

Помню, как плакал дома на улице Абая, думал, что всё упало. Родители не ругали, но я видел разочарование в их глазах. Это было больнее всего. Месяц я вообще не хотел учиться, сидел в соцсетях в парке у набережной Иртыша.

Но потом мне помогло несколько вещей. Во-первых, мой старший брат Марат поговорил со мной серьёзно — сказал, что неудача не означает конец. Во-вторых, я понял, что готовился неправильно: зубрил формулы вместо понимания. Пересдавал через три месяца, и на этот раз подготовка была другой — я разбирал задачи с Асланом, обсуждал логику, а не просто писал ответы.

Вторая попытка дала 81 балл. Я поступил. Сейчас в программе учусь на третьем семестре. Главное, что я понял: провал — это не конец, это информация. Нужно анализировать, что пошло не так, и пробовать по-другому.

Laughter, and on an One of my favorite traditions is the visit to the house of our , the . They live on eighty forested and meadowed acres outside of a quaint, old town. Their small green house overlooks brown fields and a blue pond, with tall trees forming a backdrop. We arrive midmorning. We either find our in the house or encounter them tromping out of the woods to meet us, shovels, chainsaws and other trailbuilding implements in their hands. After the customary hello, how have you been, we often wander around the yard, exclaiming at the new fruit trees or hearing stories about the latest tenants of the birdhouses. During the hottest part of the , we head for the shade of the lush woods. A short walk will bring us to a trail. I love walking among the sun-streaked ferns and fallen logs, treading carefully the rickety bridges over burbling streams, bouncing confidently on the sturdy new bridges, and trying to avoid the dogs as they galumph in and out of the water. knows all about the flora and fauna of the region, so we get a constant stream of knowledge as we hike. He also, of course, has to tell us about the trees he's planted -- a redwood here (look how well it's doing! A foot since last fall!) and a douglas fir over there (not as well. That big redwood is shading it too much). One of the best parts of the hike is when we see the dead-end section of trail that my family helped construct three years ago. We always walk to the end of it and discuss where it could go from there -- over the stream or beside it, or up the hill and if so, where would the switchbacks be? could you really bike up a trail like that? After our walk, we arrive back at the house, sweaty and talkative. Then it's time to put on swimsuits and jump in the pond! They recently built a dock that we can jump off of -- a great improvement over wading in from the edge. We swim for the majority of the , racing from one end of the pond to the other, splashing on innertubes, having pondweed-throwing battles. Finally we get tired and sit by the side of the pond, drying off in the warm sun. By , dinner is ready. Laura usually makes salmon, accompanied by a plethora of delicious side dishes. We drag chairs out to the hill above the pond and enjoy a leisurely supper. From the hill, we can see turtles and birds on the pond, bugs over the fields, and more birds swooping through the air feasting on the aforementioned bugs. After the meal, we haul chairs and dishes back to the house and sit on the porch into the . 's favorite part of the is at dusk, when the sun is at just the right angle to show all the bugs swirling through the air. At one point, all the bugs gather together and create a tornado, twisting upwards into the darkening sky, and then -- they're gone, until the next . It's an incredible spectacle; thousands of tiny insects disappering at one swoop. The best thing about these days is the friendship and comradery we have with this wonderful family. The parents knew each other long before us kids were born, so we have a lot to talk about; is very interested in science topics, and he always finds a way to bring up the latest article he read. And, as with all great , we laugh constantly. I consistently get hiccups at least three times just when we're lounging on the porch after our busy . Even on the most serious topics, my dad or the boys can find a joke to make, usually "politically incorrect" but always very funny. Now don't even get me started on the camping trips, winter ski trips or autumn cider pressing we do with the .

Nowadays, children can look on the shelves of libraries and find any type of reading you can imagine. Some magazines, books, and movies that are age appropriate. Children can also reach up on those same shelves and find some very inappropriate magazines, books, and movies. Should we remove these inappropriate items? Can we somehow get kids to not see them? Children are very curious. They want to know about everything and they will ask as many questions as they can. When they see inappropriate items on library shelves, what do we do? Libraries shouldn't get rid of items that be inappropriate for children. Instead, there should be a rating system on the books and magazines. Movies have ratings so children don't see things that are inappropriate; books should have those ratings too. If someone wants to check out something that isn't suitable for kids, then they can show the libraian their . Everybody can check out what is appropriate for their age. Libraries could even put all of the most inappropriate items in a separate section of the library. It could be a section that kids could not enter. Parents should also watch their kids to make sure they aren't getting into anything inappropriate. The only censorship they should put into libraries is rating the items by maturity. Children can look onto the shelves, but we should put labels on what they can and can't check out. Parents could look out for what their children are trying to read. I believe that's the most we can do.

Честно говоря, меня больше всего беспокоит состояние дорог в Арысе. Это не просто так говорю – каждый день вижу, как люди попадают в ямы прямо на главной улице. Несколько месяцев назад мой сосед Ерлан сломал колесо машины около рынка возле дома культуры, потому что асфальт там совсем разбитый.

Дело в том, что Арысь растет, приезжают люди с других областей, а инфраструктура не развивается так быстро. Когда едешь в сторону Туркестана или Шымкента, разница очень заметна. У нас плохие дороги в жилых районах, и это влияет на безопасность, особенно зимой, когда все замерзает.

Я учусь на программе Public Policy and Development, и мы как раз изучаем, как нужно правильно подходить к таким вопросам. Думаю, нужно не просто ремонтировать дороги, но составить долгосрочный план развития инфраструктуры Арыса. Может быть, привлечь инвестиции, провести аудит всех дорог в городе.

Это действительно важно, потому что хорошие дороги – это не только удобство, но и здоровье людей, безопасность, экономическое развитие района. Хочу после учебы работать над такими проектами.

Честно говоря, я давно мечтаю учиться именно в inVision U. Живу в Актау, и здесь с инженерией и технологиями всё сложновато. В нашем городе много нефтяных компаний, но креативный подход к инженерии – это редкость. Когда я узнал о программе Creative Engineering, сразу понял, что это то, что мне нужно.

Я планирую после окончания вернуться в Актау и работать над проектами, которые сделают нашу экономику более диверсифицированной. Для меня это не просто образование – это путь, чтобы стать полезным для своего региона и доказать, что из Актау можно вырастить серьёзных инженеров-инноваторов.

Честно говоря, самый большой вызов для меня был переход на IT Product Design. Я вообще с филологического направления пришел в школе, родители хотели, чтобы я стал учителем. В Уральске не так много возможностей для IT, поэтому я сам начал учиться программированию в 16 лет через YouTube и Coursera.

Первые полгода было ужасно. Я не понимал базовые концепции, все падало. Мой друг Ерсин из соседнего дома уже работал в веб-агентстве, он посмотрел мой код и сказал, что это дерьмо. Вместо того чтобы сдаться, я попросил его менторить меня. Мы встречались каждую субботу в кафе "Айнур" на проспекте Абулхаирова, он объяснял Figma, UI/UX принципы, взаимодействие с разработчиками.

Потом я начал делать свои проекты. Первый дизайн для приложения доставки еды в Уральске получился средненько, но это был опыт. Второй уже лучше. На третьем меня заметил мой нынешний руководитель и предложил стажировку.

Меня спасло упорство и то, что я не боялся выглядеть глупо. Я научился, что провалы — это нормально, главное не останавливаться. Сейчас я помогаю младшим ребятам, которые начинают с IT.

The -inspirational, of I the of -- . What is , exactly? Some might say, ", that's obvious. 's a sound, emitted from a person when they think something is funny!" That's as good a response as any other, and certainly quite believable. But I believe laughter has a much deeper definition; a definition that can only be explained through a marginally-humorous, less-than-inspirational story about my experiences as a -- basketball player. This year, as a high school sophomore, I decided to do something I'd never done before: go out for the basketball team. I was inspired by a longing to become more involved in the school district, and to be able to exercise throughout the rain-drenched winter months in which took place. Having only picked up a basketball in order to steer clear of the "sit-outs" zone in middle school , my performance at early practices was comparable to that of a high school dropout determining the orbit of the planets around the sun; and at least they get a calculator. Naturally the year I decided to give basketball a shot, the coaches informed us that seven unlucky individuals would be plucked from the team with joyous abandon. Through sheer force of determination, I improved enough in our first few weeks to be deemed "better than dirt" by the coaches; narrowly avoiding losing my spot on the team. In the months ahead, I would learn that my job wouldn't be making baskets and stealing balls... As astonishing as was, my ability to imagine myself playing basketball far surpassed my actual skills on the court. I soon found that my place on the team wouldn't be aggressively running up and down the court fighting for control of an orange ball; I would be on the sidelines, cheeks firmly planted on the bench upon which my teammates would take breathers before going back into the action. Our team could play basketball, but not often on the same level as the teams we faced. As each game came and went, I could see the fighting spirit fizzling out of my peers' eyes; their morale was simply dropping, and no amount of my ball-playing abilities could change that. was one game in particular twhen I discovered I didn't have to play in order to help my team. was a home game, in our lower gym; we were down by about points against a team we had fared against previously. Needless to say, players were becoming very frustrated. One of our star players, , was becoming so frustrated that our coaches decided to pull him out for a breather. He was raging, spitting profanities. He dropped himself on the bench with the elegance of an enraged walrus. His mom came down from the stands to give him water, which only made him embarrassed him more. Sitting beside , I could feel the anger radiating off of him. He was ranting under his breath over number , the opposing team's point guard. I noticed that while 's fast legs and swift hands made him a great ball-player, his voice -- a good octave above his teammates' -- was much more suited for covering songs than calling out plays. I turned towards , tapping him on the shoulder, and informed him of my insight. He looked at me for a moment, a mixture of anguish and "don't-talk-to-me-or-I-will-murder-" on his face before bursting out laughing. Clapping me on the back, he said with a smile: " always know to make us laugh, ". Suddenly dawned on me that my banter and dripping sarcasm was quite often the one thing keeping smiles on my teammates' faces. I was able to use to diffuse tense situations, and allow emotions to flow freely in a more positive manner. We lost the game. In fact, we lost all but one game the entire season; and so I made my personal duty to keep the entire team in good spirits even in the worst of times. As the weeks went by, I started to feel more and more an integral part of the team; making teammates laugh kept their minds clear of anger and frustration, and allowed them to play to the best of their abilities. And so was. Some players had quick hands, others had a flawless shot. Me? I made people laugh. I gave my peers, my friends, the ability to see light in even the most dire of situations. I didn't receive an award, a recognition of athletic ability. Instead I found the satisfaction of making people smile, of watching the enraged despair on their faces disappear -- replaced with optimism and hope. Laughter is what pushed my teammates past anger, to be the best they could be. So, tell me: Is laughter simply noise that a person makes when something is funny, or is something more? Spoiler alert: 's much, much more.

Честно говоря, самый большой вызов для меня был переход в десятый класс с казахского языка обучения на русский. Я выросла в Арысе, где большинство школ работают на казахском, и когда перевелась в гимназию номер 2, было реально сложно.

Первый семестр был адским. Я не понимала половину того, что говорит учитель математики, Аружан Ахановна объясняла на русском, а я сидела и переводила в голове каждое слово. Мои оценки упали с пятёрок на тройки, и я чувствовала себя совсем потерянной. Родители начали волноваться, особенно мама.

Но потом мне помогло несколько вещей. Во-первых, моя подруга Жанна, которая училась в этой гимназии с седьмого класса, стала мне объяснять непонятные темы после уроков. Мы сидели в столовой школы и разбирали физику, химию. Во-вторых, я начала смотреть русские фильмы и слушать музыку – это реально помогло с восприятием на слух.

К концу года я привыкла, и теперь русский мне даже нравится. Сейчас я учусь на программе Public Policy, и язык уже не проблема. Думаю, главное было не сдаваться в первый же месяц и просить помощь у друзей. Это научило меня, что трудности временные, если над ними работать.

Когда никто не смотрит, я залезаю в гараж у деда и просто разбираю старые электронные штуки. Честно, это меня затягивает на часы. Недавно нашел старый радиоприемник начала девяностых, и я потратил целый день на то, чтобы понять, как там устроены конденсаторы и катушки индуктивности. Никакого результата, просто процесс.

Еще я люблю ездить по ночам на велосипеде вдоль реки Тобол. Костанай ночью совсем другой, особенно летом. Едишь мимо парка Боровое, слышишь звуки, видишь звезды. Это как медитация для меня. Никому об этом не рассказываю, просто для себя.

И кодинг, конечно. В Creative Engineering мне нравится учиться, но дома я иногда пишу совсем бесполезные программы просто потому, что интересно. Ну, вот недавно у нас в университете была групповая работа по Digital Marketing Strategy для местного туристического проекта «Аралтөбе». Наша команда состояла из четырех человек: я, Арман, Айгуль и Нурсултан. Задача была сложная — создать полный маркетинг-план для привлечения туристов в наш регион.

Я отвечала за социальные сети и контент-стратегию, Арман делал аналитику, Айгуль работала над визуалом, а Нурсултан занимался PR. На втором этапе проекта у нас возник конфликт. Арман считал, что нужно делать упор на международную аудиторию, а я настаивала на локальном казахском рынке. Мы долго спорили, было напряженно.

Но потом мы сели, обсудили спокойно и поняли, что оба правы. Нурсултан предложил двухфазный подход: сначала привлечь казахов из Алматы и Нур-Султана, потом расширяться на международный уровень. Это был гениальный ход!

Я создала контент на казахском и русском языках, Айгуль сделала потрясающие фото наших местных памятников, и результат превзошел все ожидания. Профессор дал нам девять из десяти баллов. Это был настоящий командный успех — вместе мы создали что-то намного лучше, чем смогли бы по отдельности.

Billions of books float from shelf to shelf each day: fictional and nonfictional, horror and comedy. Writers reside in every part of the world composing works from complex life experiences to simple dreams. Being an author, who has the right to freedom of speech, story plots become to have endless combinations. Every reader seeks out a different style. Libraries contain books that tower to the ceilings, any kind, every kind. Books are divided into their individual sections according to truth, kind and cover, each category holding about four options. The necessity for censorship should never be an option. Writers compose for all sorts of people. For some to say what's 'right' or 'wrong' is not a legitamate reason for a piece of work to be removed from a shelf. If, perhaps, more books had ratings such as movies do, an cubicle could be created instead of allowing young people to have access to such vulgarity. Taking away the enjoyment for some readers, however, is unethical. Whether pertaining to books, music, magazines, etc., censorship is unnecessary. Those who compose the entertainment should not have to worry about the content of their expression and/or interpretation. If the worry is concerning youth, parental guidance should be in affect. Resulting in cancellation can affect those who relate to the source so it's important to consider all options. To each, its own.

Some people like making people laugh, I love it. I will do most anything to get a good laugh. I will make fun of my self, do insanely stupid things, and sometimes hurt myself (not in any serious way). When I was little I didn't really understand laughter. For some odd reason I could never tell the difference if people were laughing at something or laughing with it. I was kind of "special" in some areas as a kid (I still am today). Still at the tender age of five I loved making people laugh, and being special I would do even crazier things for a laugh. Mind you I was kind of a spaz, and a really big spaz. I was the most hyperactive five year old you will ever meet. For example one time I hit myself in the head with a hammer, another time I was dancing around in class with a pencil in my hand, stabbed myself in the head with it, and needed stitches. One of the craziest times though was a couple days before I had to take pictures and I wanted to go play outside, my mom knowing how "special" I was (I got it from her) wouldn't allow me to. The expert persuasive kid I was back then convinced her to let me go outside. Before I could even reach the street I fell head first on to the corner of the sidewalk leaving a huge mark and completely ruining the pictures. Although that might make some people laugh, this is a story about laughter not me being a spaz. Now that you know that I love making people laugh, I'm "special", and that I'm a complete spaz I can get on with the story. Well I was in kindergarten and I loved school because I got to hang out with my friends and play with blocks, that might sound stupid but I was in kindergarten. The only thing I didn't like about kindergarten was bully's. Surprisingly I have never had a bully except kindergarten, but this was a bad bully. He would give me wedgies at story time and the whole deal (which was the best time to do so because the teacher could couldn't see). I still know the bully too, but he's no bully anymore, he's a goody two shoes now which I think is odd. Anyways, kindergarten was a very good year for me except one day (and every day I got a wedgies). That day is what this whole story is about, it's why I told you I love making people laugh, why I told you I'm "special", and a spaz, everything in the story circles around this one day, *dramatic pause* in kindergarten. It started out like any other day in kindergarten. I woke up, did my daily routine, hopped in the car, and headed to school. When I got to school I grabbed my daily binder and patted the education sign like a mall cop would pat the observe and report sign. I did all my work and colored (which was basically all my work). It came around break so we ran around the play ground and got are little snack. When we finished getting the last few drops out of our juice boxes we headed over to story time. We were all in the little circle (which was more like a deformed oval) listening to the story, right when I would get into the story and lose my guard I would receive an excruciatingly painful (for a five year old) wedgie. The story was almost finished and our five year old attention spans were wearing thin and we were getting all excited. The story finally finished and we were standing up, and this is where my memory starts to fade. I cracked a really funny joke and the whole kindergarten class erupted into laughter, me being a "special" spaz that can't tell if people are laughing at me or with me burst into tears. I remember balling my eyes out at the drinking fountain trying to hide my tears. One of the teachers tried to help me by telling me that they were laughing at my joke. It took me a couple minutes to stop crying but a little longer to realize the were not laughing at me. To this day I still get reminded by classmates about that day, of course I can laugh about it now but that was in kindergarten, I'm in ninth grade now and for people to remember that is kind of crazy to me. It was a negative experience then, but it turned into a blessing in disguise. It made me grow into a better person, I can tell the difference of laughter and also be okay when people do laugh at me (doing dumb things to make people laugh at me is actually my forte). So remember, being "special" could sometimes be the best thing about you, what makes you who you are, what makes you great, what makes you grow, what makes people laugh.

Для меня лидерство — это не просто командовать, а вдохновлять людей на что-то большее. Это когда ты берёшь ответственность и показываешь путь другим своим примером.

У нас в университете я возглавляю Digital Marketing Club уже второй год. Когда я пришёл на первое собрание, там было человек пятнадцать, и все просто сидели без идей. По моей инициативе мы запустили проект по продвижению местных уральских брендов в соцсетях. Я предложил команде создавать контент для TikTok и Instagram, и ребята загорелись идеей.

За три месяца мы выросли до сорока активных членов клуба. Мы сделали серию роликов о кафе «Апельсин» на проспекте Абая и магазинах на Достыка — результаты были реальные: один владелец кафе сказал, что благодаря нашему контенту к нему приходит на двадцать процентов больше молодёжи. Это было крутко.

Я понял, что лидерство — это когда ты не просто даёшь задачи, а вместе работаешь, поддерживаешь каждого. Мой друг Дамир сначала боялся снимать видео, но я помог ему, и теперь он лучший видеограф в клубе. Вот это для меня настоящее лидерство — помочь людям раскрыть свой потенциал и добиться результатов вместе.

Вот, у нас в университете была проектная работа по городскому развитию Костаная. Наша команда из пяти человек должна была разработать план реновации центра города. Я был координатором и отвечал за связь между подгруппами.

Сначала пошло напряженно. Айнур, которая занималась исследованиями, и Тимур, отвечавший за дизайн, постоянно спорили о концепции. Айнур хотела сохранить историческую часть около памятника Абая, а Тимур предлагал полный редизайн. Я предложил встречу в кафе на проспекте Аль-Фараби и предложил компромисс – сохранить историческое ядро, но модернизировать инфраструктуру вокруг.

Остальные двое, Данияр и Мадина, занимались экономическими расчетами и социальными опросами. Когда я собрал все части вместе, получилось нечто большее. План включал не только архитектурные решения, но и экономическое обоснование, и мнение жителей Костаная.

Преподаватель Гульнара Сергеевна дала нам девять из десяти. Она сказала, что это был пример настоящей командной работы. Мы поняли, что каждый вносит что-то важное, и конфликты – это нормально, если их правильно разрешать.

Недавно на втором курсе мы работали над проектом для нашего предмета Digital Strategy. Нужно было создать маркетинговую кампанию для одного из местных бизнесов в Актау. Нас было четверо в группе: я, Айнур, Нурлан и Дина.

Задача была сложная – нужно было провести анализ конкурентов, создать контент для социальных сетей и подготовить презентацию. Я отвечала за работу с Instagram и TikTok. Сначала было трудно, потому что ребята хотели одно, а я видела совсем другой подход к контенту. Например, Нурлан предлагал много текста в постах, а я настаивала на визуальном контенте, потому что это работает лучше для молодой аудитории.

Мы спорили около недели, но потом Айнур предложила компромисс – делать короткие, яркие посты с крючками в начале. Я также помогала ребятам с идеями контента, потому что хорошо знаю, что нравится людям в нашем городе.

В итоге наша работа получила самую высокую оценку. Преподаватель отметил именно нашу социальную стратегию. Это показало мне, что даже когда не согласны, нужно слушать друг друга и искать решение вместе.

Для меня лидерство — это не просто командовать людьми, а помогать им двигаться в одном направлении и верить в результат. Я понимаю это через свой опыт в программе Creative Engineering.

В прошлом году мы работали над проектом робота для сортировки отходов. Я был назначен координатором нашей группы из пяти человек. Честно говоря, вначале я не уверен был в своих способностях — ребята были опытнее меня. Но я старался слушать каждого: Айдара, который разбирается в электронике, Марию из лицея №1, которая предложила классный дизайн, и двух младших ребят из девятого класса.

Мне удалось организовать встречи по вторникам в техноклубе при школе №12, распределить задачи честно. Когда у нас не работал датчик в апреле, я помог команде не отчаиваться — мы переделали всё за две недели. Проект занял третье место на областной выставке в Петропавловске.

Может быть, это не огромный успех, но я понял главное: лидер должен верить в людей и создавать условия, чтобы каждый внёс свой вклад. Это научило меня быть ответственнее и лучше слышать других.

If this is the case, they should be mature enough to handle stumbling across the material, and or making the decision to put the book back and to not continue reading. Saying that the material is unsuitable for a younger age group is correct, but at that age the children should be with adult when checking out books anyway. The material that people find unacceptable would almost certainly be in a novel that is intended for a mature audience, so if it is being read by a younger age group that would be the problem in and of it's self. The libraries should not be put on a cencorship, but open to the public that wish to dive in to these stories. Books are written for a purpose, and that purpose just be to let people know that these things are happening, and if one thinks they are alone in these strifes that they are not

Я работал в команде над проектом по развитию социальной политики в Атырау. Это было в рамках нашей программы Public Policy and Development в университете. Нас было четверо: я, Айнур, Нурлан и Дина.

Задача была сложная – нужно было разработать программу поддержки малого бизнеса в нефтяной промышленности для молодёжи нашего города. Я отвечал за исследование и анализ данных, Айнур работал над законодательной базой, Нурлан – за экономическими расчётами, а Дина координировала встречи с местными предпринимателями.

На третьей неделе начались проблемы. Нурлан считал, что наши предложения по финансированию нереалистичны, а Айнур настаивал на более строгих требованиях. Я предложил провести совместное обсуждение с экспертом из управления экономического развития Атырау. Результат превзошёл наши ожидания. Наш проект заметили в администрации города, и его даже рассмотрели как основу для реальной программы поддержки. Это научило меня, что в команде разные мнения – это сила, если уметь их объединить.

Главная причина в том, что у нас много нефтеперерабатывающих предприятий, а контроль за выбросами не очень строгий. Это влияет на здоровье не только детей, но и пожилых людей. Моя бабушка говорит, что раньше в Актобе было чище.

Лидерство для меня – это не про то, чтобы командовать людьми, а про ответственность и умение вести за собой. Я понял это на практике в нашей программе Creative Engineering.

В начале второго семестра наш преподаватель Алмас Амирович поручил мне координировать проект по разработке мобильного приложения для местного бизнеса. В группе было пятеро ребят: Ерсултан, Диана, Марат и Даниил. Честно, я не чувствовал себя суперлидером, но старался держать всё в порядке.

Организовал встречи каждый вторник в кафе неподалеку от университета на улице Валиханова. Там мы обсуждали сроки, распределяли задачи. Когда Ерсултан отстал с фронтенд-частью в третью неделю, я не стал его ругать, а помог разобраться в React вместе. Диана отвечала за дизайн, и я следил, чтобы её идеи совпадали с техническими возможностями.

В итоге мы сдали проект вовремя, и приложение даже заинтересовало одну небольшую компанию в Таразе. Не суперуспех, конечно, но я понял: лидерство – это когда ты помогаешь людям раскрыть свой потенциал и вместе двигаетесь к цели. Это про доверие и ответственность перед командой.

Для меня лидерство – это не обязательно быть самым громким в комнате, а скорее брать ответственность за то, чтобы люди вокруг чувствовали себя услышанными. В нашем Арысе это особенно важно, потому что в небольшом городе каждый знает друг друга.

Вот конкретный пример. В прошлом году я учился в школе номер 5, и я заметил, что многие ребята не ходят на кружки просто потому, что не знают, как туда попасть или стесняются. Мой учитель истории, Асхат Сериков, попросил меня помочь организовать информационный день о внеклассных занятиях. Я согласился, хотя это был мой первый опыт.

Я составил список всех кружков в центре, попросил руководителей подготовить короткие презентации и помог ребятам задавать вопросы. Ничего супергеройского – просто связал людей между собой. В результате на кружки записалось около сорока человек, особенно много стало на дебаты и экологический клуб.

Это научило меня, что лидерство – это не власть, а помощь другим найти свой путь. Сейчас я изучаю Public Policy именно потому, что хочу развивать эту способность на уровне целых сообществ. Даже в маленьком городе можно сделать что-то полезное.

Самый большой вызов для меня был поступить в университет. Я живу в Костанае, и когда я готовилась к ЕНТ в 2021 году, я провалила первую попытку. Набрала всего 78 баллов, а нужно было минимум 95 для Public Policy. Это была ужасная ночь, я плакала дома, мама пыталась меня утешить, но я чувствовала себя полной неудачницей.

Но мой папа сказал мне что-то важное: «Айгерим, ты не первая, кто не прошёл с первого раза. Это не конец». Я решила учиться дальше. Во второй раз набрала 91 балл — всё ещё не хватало. Было грустно, но я уже не сдавалась.

Третья попытка в 2022 году — 103 балла! Я поступила в КарГУ им. Букетова на программу Public Policy.

Эта история научила меня, что неудача — это не финал. Я научилась упорству, умению анализировать свои ошибки и не зависеть от первого результата. Теперь я знаю, что смогу преодолеть любые препятствия, если буду работать систематически и верить в себя.
